content:
SELECTED_INDEX: 8
CONFIDENCE: 0.23
EXPLANATION: Strong CH-stretching pair at 2862 / 2930 cm⁻¹ together with the intense 1446 cm⁻¹ CH₂ scissoring, 1264-1278 cm⁻¹ CH₂ twisting and a very strong 720 cm⁻¹ rocking band indicate an aliphatic, mainly ‑CH₂- containing molecule.  
The key diagnostic band is the intense 914 cm⁻¹ peak, characteristic for the symmetric ring breathing / C–O–C stretch of a five- to six-membered cyclic ether; accompanying C–O stretches appear at 1043 and 1075 cm⁻¹. The doublet at 834 / 851 cm⁻¹ also matches reported ring modes of tetrahydropyran derivatives.  
Among the candidates only compound 8 (CC1CCCCOC1C), a dimethyl-substituted tetrahydropyran, possesses such a six-membered cyclic ether skeleton and enough consecutive CH₂ groups to account for the very strong 720 cm⁻¹ rocking band, while avoiding O–H or C=O groups (no Raman evidence for OH or C=O stretches). The other O-containing candidates have smaller (oxetane) or more constrained bicyclic rings, or contain alcohol functions that should give detectable O–H stretching bands. Therefore candidate 8 provides the best agreement with the observed Raman pattern.
